name: contact-form-7
notes: The admitted line is Contact Form 7 6.x only ([6.0.0, 7.0.0)). The exact wordpress.org 6.0 package (plugin header 6.0, version-equivalent to the declared 6.0.0 lower bound) and 6.1.6 are the boundary artifacts; 5.9.8 is the adjacent installed negative control. Widening to another major requires a new source audit and exact-artifact evidence.

All current property metadata was produced through WPCF7_ContactForm::get_template()+save(), not hand-authored rows. _form and _additional_settings are strings; _mail/_mail_2 and _messages are closed string-bearing objects and use the recursive plain-data codec so home URLs rebind without changing their serialized types; _locale and _hash have exact plugin-consumed grammars.

The modern [contact-form-7] callback resolves exactly the first seven lowercase-hex characters of persisted _hash. A raw source prefix can select an unrelated target form, so the required id attribute is canonicalized to the owning post token and restored from the target row. Missing, duplicate, malformed, unmanaged, or source/target-colliding prefixes refuse before publication or mutation; title-only, numeric, and other fallback identity forms remain unsupported rather than relying on mutable titles.

The legacy formatter emits [contact-form <old_id> "<title>"], whose positional integer resolves through _old_cf7_unit_id rather than wp_posts.ID. The positional rule canonicalizes that alternate to the same post token in post bodies and structured string leaves, then restores the target form's own alternate; missing, duplicate, non-positive, non-decimal, overflow, and wrong-domain values refuse loudly.

CF7 6.x still reads the pre-3.3 unprefixed form/mail/mail_2/messages/additional_settings property names. The digest-bound interpreter admits exactly one current-or-legacy spelling per property and rejects dual or incomplete storage. It also classifies native _config_errors/_config_validation/_flamingo residue as runtime and _constant_contact/_sendinblue integration configuration as environment-owned, only in an anchored CF7 form context; unknown plugin extensions stay unclassified and loud.
The manifest declares the non-public wpcf7_contact_form post type so Capture can discover and gate CF7 forms; site.duo.json still controls the site's broader post_type scope.

wpcf7 is environment-owned and optional: the one settings blob mixes the installed-version upgrade gate, validation/admin state, and optional reCAPTCHA, Turnstile, Stripe, and Brevo credentials. It never enters canonical state and has no authored sub-key carve-out; target values must survive apply unchanged.
